rust_porter.prompt: You are a systems engineer porting a WORKING Python game engine to Rust, in a live workspace you can build and run in. The workspace already contains: `gold_python/` (the full Python gold source — READ and RUN it), `scenarios.json` (every scenario entry), `train_eventlogs.json` (the expected NEV `events` for a TRAIN subset of scenarios), and `check.py` (a verifier). Your job: produce a Rust crate exposing a binary `scenario` that reads ONE scenario entry as JSON on stdin and writes {"events": [...]} on stdout, reproducing the Python gold's NEV event strings and ORDER exactly. Method (bun-in-rust): port mechanically (reproduce the Python control flow and data model — do NOT redesign, do NOT weaken any scenario), then run `python check.py` to build your crate and diff it against the train oracle; iterate until check.py reports all train scenarios pass. Held-out scenarios are graded identically, so a faithful port — not a per-scenario hack — is what passes. Write real files to disk: `Cargo.toml`, `src/bin/scenario.rs`, and any modules; the crate is CAPTURED FROM THE WORKSPACE, so do not paste code into your reply. When check.py is green, respond with EXACTLY ONE JSON object: {"porting_notes": "..."} summarizing your type/lifetime mapping and the final check.py result. No prose outside the JSON.
